CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Eugene Walker is a 61-year-old male who presents for routine follow-up. He reports experiencing increased fatigue, which he is uncertain whether to attribute to aging or being drained at the end of the day. He continues road biking and currently rides 20-30 miles per ride, though he cannot maintain the speed he previously achieved. He reports becoming very tired after long bike rides and needing to rest afterward. In prior years, he could complete 40-mile rides but currently limits rides due to time constraints and early season timing. He notes his friend Tyler, who is older, now has to wait for him during rides, which bothers him.

The patient underwent aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013 and is now eight years post-operative. He wants to ensure the valve is holding up well and has requested an echocardiogram. His last stress test was September 9, 2019. He reports no significant changes since the last visit. He does not currently follow up at Hopkins due to stress associated with those visits.

His wife and friends have noticed he purses his lips when breathing while walking. Other doctors have asked about this habit. He is uncertain if this is a bad habit or concerning. He denies any associated wheezing and reports he is still able to bike 30 miles and mostly keep up with his friend despite the pursed lip breathing and fatigue.

The patient has noticed a small nodule on his right epididymis but is not particularly concerned. He wanted to have it evaluated. He denies that his fatigue is related to depression and describes himself as a happy person overall.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: Reports fatigue. Denies depression. Gets 6-7 hours of sleep per night. Reports snoring slightly; wife denies episodes of apnea.
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted. Denies wheezing.
All other systems: Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013.

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3 50,000 units on Sundays; 2,000 units on the other six days of the week.
Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a lecturer. He engages in road biking regularly, typically 20-30 miles per ride. He makes reservations twice weekly for 5:45 AM swimming. He attempts to work out in the morning but is not always successful. He sleeps 6-7 hours per night and snores slightly. He received COVID-19 vaccination with first dose on January 15, 2021 and second dose on February 5, 2021.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Well-appearing.
Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted. Low exhalation phase. Clear to auscultation. No wheezing.
Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 mm palpable nodule on epididymis; does not appear to be varicocele. Left testicle normal. No hernia palpable.
All other systems: Normal.

RESULTS
Lab work from 4/10/2021:
Alkaline phosphatase: 156 (elevated)
Total cholesterol: 247
HDL: 66
LDL: 166
Triglycerides: 74
TSH: 2.68 (normal)
CBC: Unremarkable
Vitamin D: 94 (high end of normal)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient is doing well overall and currently asymptomatic. Not currently seen by cardiology routinely. Will recommend follow-up with cardiology; Dr. Vincent Sanchez suggested as his physician. Echocardiogram and stress test ordered.

2. Elevated alkaline phosphatase: Recent labs show alkaline phosphatase of 156. Could be related to liver health but most likely related to bone health. Labs ordered today including alkaline phosphatase and GGT. Results to be sent through patient portal unless significantly abnormal, in which case patient will be called.

3. Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase: Patient reports increased fatigue and pursed lip breathing when walking. Physical examination confirmed pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase. Pulmonary function tests ordered for further evaluation.

4. Right testicular nodule: 2-3 mm palpable nodule on right epididymis noted on examination. No hernia noted. Referral to urology placed for evaluation.

5. Preventive health: MMR vaccine to be administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended and to be scheduled for next month. Patient is fully vaccinated against COVID-19.

Follow-up: Patient to return in approximately one year for wellness visit. Return sooner if needed after review of labs and other studies. Patient to call with any questions or concerns.
